title: Tariffs, Liquidity, Bitcoin, and Lat Am Equities
summary: Tariff incidence, Bitcoin confidence and Latin American value.
assessment: The Copa and Itaú entries produced favorable returns, while the renewed Bitcoin floor and cycle confidence failed to protect against a substantial drawdown. Stablecoin adoption is separated usefully from token value capture. Tariff incidence is mostly domestic, but the consumer-versus-business split is overstated.

claims.claim: Tariff escalation followed the prior warning.
claims.reason: The July tariff letters and subsequent country-rate order support the predicted return of negotiations and threats. This is the same July policy episode as report 166, not another independent forecasting win.
claims.direction_assessment: See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

claims.claim: US consumers bear most tariff costs.
claims.reason: Later research supports a predominantly domestic burden across firms and consumers, with nearly 90% borne domestically. It does not support simply ranking consumers first: New York Fed research estimates about 26% pass-through to consumer prices. AI answers are research leads, not independent empirical evidence.

evidence.title: More tariff pass-through is in the pipeline
evidence.finding: Domestic firms and consumers bear nearly 90% of the burden.

evidence.title: Anatomy of tariff pass-through
evidence.finding: Estimates about 26% pass-through to consumer prices.

claims.claim: Leading indicators overstate recession risk.
claims.reason: The warning against treating the LEI as a deterministic recession rule is sound. Fiscal support is a possible reason for false signals, but proving it requires separating fiscal effects from services composition, pandemic distortions and indicator design. Initial claims are administrative but still revised and seasonally adjusted.

claims.claim: Claims below 300,000 suggest contained layoffs.
claims.reason: The threshold is a heuristic, not an invariant recession boundary. Population growth, unemployment-insurance eligibility, hiring weakness and labor-force exits all matter. A low layoff rate can coexist with weak job creation.

claims.claim: Bank reserves appear adequate near term.
claims.reason: No immediate crisis followed, while late-year funding pressure did emerge as the TGA rebuilt and runoff continued. Aggregate cash ratios can hide distributional shortages and regulatory constraints. The evolving interpretation is more useful than a fixed historical threshold.

claims.claim: Bill issuance is more liquidity-friendly than coupons.
claims.reason: Bills can attract money-market cash from reverse repos and therefore drain fewer bank reserves than alternative funding. The result depends on who buys them. Tariff receipts also drain private balances when collected, so reduced issuance alone does not establish a net liquidity benefit.

claims.claim: QT will give way to Treasury purchases.
claims.reason: Runoff stopped in December 2025 and reserve-management purchases began that month. MBS principal was redirected into Treasury bills. The New York Fed projection was a scenario, not a binding promise to keep assets exactly at 20% of GDP.

evidence.title: Reserve management purchase announcement
evidence.finding: Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

claims.reason: The all-737 family description is correct, and operational standardization can reduce complexity. The stated 106 aircraft is stale: Copa reported 112 in Q1 2025. claims.claim: Small uncorrelated positions can reduce portfolio risk.
claims.reason: Diversification can reduce variance when the new asset’s covariance with the portfolio is sufficiently low relative to its weight and volatility. Small size alone is insufficient, and correlations can rise during stress. The report appropriately treats airline-specific downside as a sizing concern.

proof.derivation: Portfolio variance equals the weighted variances plus twice weighted covariances; low covariance can offset added standalone variance.
